title: Where Things Are
bigQuestion: How can a drawing help us find our way?

story.title: The Treasure Map
story.kicker: The class hid a treasure. Now they must draw a map so a friend can find it.
paragraphs: Room 12 is quiet. Ms. Ortiz holds up a small gold box. "This is our treasure," she says. "Jamal will hide it. Then we will draw a map. The map will show Priya where it is." Priya waits in the hall.

Jamal hides the box under the reading rug. Now the class draws. They draw the room as if they were birds looking down. A big square is the rug. Small squares are the desks. A long shape is the teacher's table.
Sofia draws a star where the box is. Leo draws a little door. Ms. Ortiz writes a key on the side. It says: star means treasure. Square means desk. Now the map is done.
Priya comes in. She looks at the map. She finds the door. She finds the desks. She walks to the big square. She lifts the rug. There is the gold box! The map worked.
story.think: What did the class draw on the map? What did they leave out?

lessons.title: Looking Down on a Room
lessons.mainIdea: A map is a drawing of a place as seen from above.
reading: Think of a bird. It flies over your classroom. It looks down. It sees the tops of the desks. It sees the top of the rug. It does not see the legs of the chairs. It sees the room from above.
A *map* is a drawing of a place from above. It shows where things are. A map of your room shows the desks, the door and the rug. It shows them the way a bird sees them.
A map is not a photo. It is simpler. It leaves out small things. It keeps the big things. That makes it easy to read.

words.d: a drawing of a place as seen from above

look.title: Your Desk From Above
look.text: Look at your desk. Now stand up. Look down at it. You see the top. You see a book. You see a pencil. You do not see the legs. That is how a map sees things.
look.prompt: What would you draw if you made a map of your desk?

check.q: A map shows a place from where?
choices: From the side, like a photo
check.why: A map is a drawing of a place from above. It shows things the way a bird sees them.

check.q: What would a map of a room show?
choices: Where the desks and rug are
check.why: A map shows where things are. From above, you see the tops of desks and the rug.

check.q: Why is a map easier to read than a photo?
check.why: A map is simpler than a photo. It keeps the big things and leaves out the small things.

lessons.title: The Map Key
lessons.mainIdea: A map key tells what each symbol on a map means.
reading: Look at the treasure map. There is a star on it. What does the star mean? You cannot tell. So the class made a *key*. The key says: star means treasure. Now you know.
A *symbol* is a small picture that stands for something. A square can stand for a desk. A star can stand for treasure. A wavy line can stand for water. Symbols keep the map simple.
The key is a list. It shows each symbol. Next to it, it says what the symbol means. Always read the key first. Then you can read the map.

words.d: a small picture that stands for something on a map
the list on a map that tells what each symbol means

look.title: A Key for the Playground
look.text: A map of the playground has three symbols. A circle. A triangle. A long line. The key says: circle means swing. Triangle means slide. Long line means fence. Now look at the map. There are two circles by the fence.
look.prompt: What is by the fence on this playground?

check.q: What does a map key do?
choices: It tells what each symbol means
check.why: The key is a list of symbols. It tells what each one stands for.

check.q: On the class map, a star stands for what?
check.why: The class wrote the key. It said: star means treasure.

check.q: What should you read first on a map?
check.why: Read the key first. Then you know what every symbol on the map means.

lessons.title: Bigger and Bigger Maps
lessons.mainIdea: A map can show a room, a school or a whole neighborhood.
reading: A map can show a small place. Your room. A map can show a bigger place. Your whole school. On a school map, each room is a small box. The gym is a big box. The hall is a long line.
A map can show a *neighborhood*. That is the streets and homes around your school. On this map, the school is one small box. The streets are lines. The park is a green shape.
The bigger the place, the smaller each thing looks. On the room map, your desk is a square. On the school map, your whole room is a square. On the neighborhood map, the school is a square.

words.d: the streets, homes and stores around a place

look.title: How Many Squares on Each Map?
look.prompt: The neighborhood map has 40 squares. What might each square be?

check.q: On a school map, what is each room?
check.why: On a school map, each room is a small box. The hall is a long line.

check.q: What does a neighborhood map show?
choices: The streets and homes around the school
check.why: A neighborhood is the streets and homes around a place. The map shows all of them.

check.q: As a map shows a bigger place, each thing looks…
check.why: The bigger the place, the smaller each thing looks. A whole school can be one square.

lessons.title: Near, Far, Left and Right
lessons.mainIdea: Words like near, far, left and right tell where a thing is.
reading: Priya looks at the treasure map. The star is *near* the rug. It is *far* from the door. Near means close. Far means a long way off. These words help her find the box.
Left and right help too. Hold up your left hand. Now your right hand. On the map, the door is on the left. The windows are on the right. Priya walks to the right side of the room.
Use these words when you give directions. "The book is near the sink." "The ball is far from the fence." "Turn left at the door." Then a friend can find the way.

look.title: Where Is the Cat?
look.text: Look at a picture of a yard. A cat sits on the left. It is near a tree. A dog sits on the right. It is far from the tree. A ball sits in the middle. The cat is close to the ball. The dog is not.
look.prompt: Is the dog near the tree or far from it? How do you know?

check.q: Near means what?
check.why: Near means close. Far means a long way off.

check.q: On the treasure map, the star was far from what?
check.why: The star was near the rug and far from the door.

check.q: A friend says, "Turn left at the door." What kind of word is left?
check.why: Left and right are direction words. They tell which way to go.

lessons.title: North, South, East and West
lessons.mainIdea: North, south, east and west are the four main directions on a map.
reading: Left and right can change. Turn around, and left is now right! So map makers use four words that never change. *North*. *South*. East. West. On most maps, north is at the top.
Here is a trick. The sun comes up in the east. It goes down in the west. Face the sunrise. East is in front of you. West is behind you. North is on your left. South is on your right.
Maps often have a small cross with the letters N, S, E, W. Find it. Then you know which way is north. Then you can find every other direction too.

words.d: the direction at the top of most maps
the direction at the bottom of most maps

look.title: The Sun in the Morning
look.text: It is morning. Ana stands in her yard. The sun is just coming up. She faces it. Now east is in front of her. Her house is behind her. Her left hand points to the park.
look.prompt: Which direction is the park from Ana? Which direction is her house?

check.q: On most maps, which direction is at the top?
check.why: On most maps, north is at the top. South is at the bottom.

check.q: Where does the sun come up?
check.why: The sun comes up in the east. It goes down in the west.

check.q: Why do map makers use north and south instead of left and right?
choices: They never change when you turn
check.why: Left and right change when you turn around. North, south, east and west stay the same.

lessons.title: The Globe Is a Model of Earth
lessons.mainIdea: A globe is a round model of Earth that shows land and water.
reading: Earth is very big. It is round like a ball. We cannot see all of it at once. So people made a *globe*. A globe is a small model of Earth. You can spin it. You can hold it.
Look at a globe. Most of it is blue. Blue means water. The big blue parts are oceans. The green and brown parts are *land*. There is more water than land on Earth.
A flat map of the world shows the same thing. Blue is water. Green or brown is land. Rivers are thin blue lines. Lakes are blue shapes with land all around.

words.d: the dry parts of Earth, where we walk and build

look.title: Water and Land on Earth
look.prompt: Are there more water parts or more land parts? What color will most of a globe be?

check.q: What is a globe?
choices: A kind of ball for games
check.why: A globe is a small round model of Earth. You can spin it and hold it.

check.q: On a globe, what does blue mean?
check.why: Blue shows water. The big blue parts are oceans.

check.q: Which is there more of on Earth?
check.why: Most of a globe is blue. There is more water than land on Earth.

lessons.title: Finding Our Home
lessons.mainIdea: We live in Chicago, in the state of Illinois, in the United States.
reading: Find the United States on a globe. It is a big country. It is in the top half of the globe. It has an ocean on its left side and an ocean on its right side. That is our *country*.
The United States has fifty *states*. One is Illinois. Find it in the middle of the country. It is tall and thin. A big lake touches its top right corner. That lake is Lake Michigan.
Chicago is a city in Illinois. It sits right on Lake Michigan. On a map, it is a dot near the top of the state. Many people live in that dot. Maybe you do too.

words.d: a big land with its own name and its own leaders
one part of the United States, like Illinois

look.title: Zooming In
look.text: Start with the whole globe. Find the United States. Now zoom in. Find Illinois in the middle. Now zoom in more. Find the big lake in the corner. Find the dot on the lake. That dot is Chicago. Zoom in again. Somewhere in that dot is your school.
look.prompt: Which is bigger, Illinois or Chicago? How can you tell from the map?

check.q: Illinois is a…
check.why: Illinois is one of the fifty states in the United States.

check.q: What big lake touches Chicago?
check.why: Chicago sits right on Lake Michigan. The lake touches the top right corner of Illinois.

check.q: Which is the biggest?
check.why: The United States is a country. Illinois is one state inside it. Chicago is one city inside Illinois.

lessons.title: A Route to School
lessons.mainIdea: A route is the path you take to get from one place to another.
reading: Leo walks to school. He leaves his door. He turns right. He walks past the store. He turns left at the park. He crosses the street at the light. Then he is at school. That is his *route*.
A route is the path from one place to another. You can draw it on a map. Start at home. Draw a line. Follow the streets. End at school. Mark the turns.
A good route map tells you where to turn. It shows the things you pass. The store. The park. The light. Those things help you know you are going the right way.

words.d: the path you take from one place to another

look.title: Two Ways to the Park
look.text: Mia can go two ways to the park. Way one: go straight up her street. It is short. Way two: go past the library, then turn left. It is longer. But it has a sidewalk the whole way. Mia's mom picks way two.
look.prompt: Why might Mia's mom pick the longer route?

check.q: What is a route?
choices: A path from one place to another
check.why: A route is the path you take to get from one place to another.

check.q: Where did Leo turn left?
check.why: Leo turned right at his door. He turned left at the park.

check.q: What helps you know you are going the right way?
choices: The things you pass, like the store
check.why: A good route map shows the things you pass. Seeing them tells you that you are on the right path.

review.q: A map is a drawing of a place from…
review.why: A map shows a place from above, the way a bird sees it.

review.q: What tells you what a star on a map means?
review.why: The key lists each symbol and tells what it means.

review.q: The sun comes up in the…
review.why: The sun comes up in the east and goes down in the west.
A globe is a small round model of Earth. Most of it is blue for water.

review.q: Chicago is a city in which state?
review.why: Chicago is a city in the state of Illinois. The United States is the country.

review.q: On a route map, what should you mark?
choices: The turns and the things you pass
review.why: A route map shows where to turn and what you pass along the way.
